There is one shrine of this name each in {{ill|Habikino|Q694308|qid=Q694308}} and {{ill|Kashiwara|Q873583|qid=Q873583}}; both are {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} of "Morimoto Shrine, two seats," a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}) of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Asuka District}} in {{ill|Kawachi Province|be|Каваты (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Kawachi|ckb|پارێزگای کاواچی|cs|Provincie Kawači|de|Provinz Kawachi|es|Provincia de Kawachi|fa|ولایت کاواچی|fr|Province de Kawachi|gl|Provincia de Kawachi|hak|Kawachi-koet|id|Provinsi Kawachi|it|Kawachi (provincia)|ja|河内国|ko|가와치국|lt|Kavačio žemė|nl|Kawachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Kawachi|ru|Кавати (провинция)|simple|Kawachi Province|sk|Kawači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Кавачи|tr|Kawachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Каваті|zh|河內國|zh_min_nan|Kawati-kok|zh_yue|河內國|qid=Q1047150}}. The Habikino Morimoto Shrine is considered the stronger candidate. It is said to grant blessings for cutting/enjoining relationships, naming, and divination. {{nihongo|'''Morimoto Shrine'''|杜本神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

== Overview ==
Both include {{ill|Futsunushi|fr|Futsunushi|it|Futsunushi|ja|経津主神|mni|ꯐꯨꯠꯁꯨꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Futsunushi|ru|Фуцунуси|zh|經津主神|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi}} among their enshrined deities. One theory says that in the era of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, Iwawakino-Mikoto, 14th-generation descendant of Futsunushi-no-Mikoto, lived at the place of Futsunushi's tomb and enshrined the ancestral deity there.

Besides being recorded as a myojin taisha in the Engishiki Jinmyocho, its festival is listed in the Engishiki as "Morimoto Festival," and emissaries from the Treasury Bureau attended. During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era, when {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} attacked {{ill|Takaya Castle|Q11669272|qid=Q11669272}}, shrine buildings and treasures were lost in war fire; in {{ill|1586|Q6739|qid=Q6739}} (Tensho 14), lands were confiscated by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}}, causing decline.

== Enshrined deities ==
It is said to enshrine the married pair Futsunushi-no-Mikoto and Futsunushi-hime-no-Mikoto, but ''Shrine Register'' records {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} and Futsunushi-no-Mikoto; ''Kawachi no Kuni Shikijin Shiko'' lists {{ill|Kukunochi|Q10749920|qid=Q10749920|lt=Kukunochi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|qid=Q8191796|lt=Hiyatani-ni-imasu Mizuhanome-no-Kami}}; ''Place Name Dictionary,'' ''Jingi Shiryo,'' and ''Chiri Shiryo'' call it "the ancestral deity of the Tosoki no Sukune clan."

== History ==
The founding date is unknown. Shrine tradition says the clan related to Iwawakino-Mikoto conducted rites, and in the Heian period called themselves "Yahagi Imiki." In the era of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}, shrine-temple Kongorin-ji was founded and served by shrine monks, but it was abolished by {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} in Meiji. It was ranked village shrine in Meiji 5 (1872), and became a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shinsen-heihaku-ryo kyoshinsha}} in Meiji 41 ({{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}).

== Precincts ==
In front of the main hall stand a pair of stone objects called "Hayato stones." They are beast-head human-body carvings; date unknown, but closely resemble the first Hayato stone at "Nafuyama Tomb" in {{ill|Nara (city)|Q169134|qid=Q169134}}<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title="Hayato Stone"|url=https://www.city.habikino.lg.jp/soshiki/shougaigakushu/bunkazaihogoka/bunkazai/iseki_shokai/kaisetsu/2466.html|website=Habikino City|accessdate=2019-10-04|language=ja}}</ref>.

== Subsidiary shrines ==
The current shrine building was moved in from {{ill|Kōzu-gū|Q11671792|qid=Q11671792}} in the Edo period. Precinct shrines include:

* Idaya Wakamiya (Wakamiya Shrine) - deities: {{ill|Emperor Hanzei|Q329769|qid=Q329769}}, Iwawakino-Mikoto, Otome-no-Mikoto.
* Nanki Shrine - deity: Senior First Rank Tachibana no Ason {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|Q382234|qid=Q382234}}.
* Tenmangu
* Amateru Kotai Shrine
* Mitsukuni Inari Shrine
* Mitsuyoshi Inari Shrine

Only one deity, Futsunushi-no-Mikoto, is enshrined; however, ''Meiji Shrine Register'' states "deity unknown."

The founding date is unknown. Its Meiji-era rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Unranked Shrine}}. On December 25, Meiji 40 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}), it was merged into {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokubu Shrine}} (Kokubu Ichiba, Kashiwara) and became a precinct shrine there. In March Showa 47 ({{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}}), shrine buildings were rebuilt at the former site. A precinct shrine (Morimoto Shrine) inside Kokubu Shrine still exists.
